GoalAttentionEntry.description: Goals.ReadModel.attention/1 entry as served; the goal surface re-reads the full projection for detail.

ProjectBlockedEntry.description: The shell's existing project-level blocked item, plus the project identity needed to render it beside Goal attention.

ReadUnavailable.description: Set when one feed could not be read. The page still serves the other feed with HTTP 200; the code is the server's mapped error code, never a fabricated reason.

attention-read.schema.json.description: Members of the Portal attention read: the existing server-side Goal attention feed merged with the project-level blocked work items the workspace read already serves. Every member this read requires is one the served projection always emits (a served null stays nullable), whether or not a surface reads it, so omitting or renaming one cannot pass every gate while the page silently renders a zero or a fallback; served members this read leaves optional stay additive, and every policy member (attention reasons, blockers, readiness) is the server's own projection, never a client derivation.

ChatCommand.description: Protocol.command/1 as embedded in a chat message receipt. Task-scoped commands (a cancel or retry recorded before any run exists) carry run_id and generation as null; run-scoped commands carry both.

ChatMessage.description: Chat.message_json/1: one durable conversation message as served in the scoped page, oldest first. discuss and status questions never create a command, so command stays null for them.

ChatRun.description: Chat.ReadModel.runs/2 entry: the work detail projection behind one scoped work item, newest first and capped at the read model's run limit. raw.timeline is blanked to [] while keeping the same members because the chat read serves no raw history rows; the work detail endpoint remains the diagnostic surface for raw events.

TaskRead.description: Protocol.task/1 as served for the work item snapshot.

TimelineCommandData.description: Timeline command receipt with run_id and generation removed by Protocol.timeline_data/2.

TimelineEventData.description: Timeline event payload with run identity removed by Protocol.timeline_data/2.

TimelineTransitionData.description: Timeline transition payload with run identity removed by Protocol.timeline_data/2.

WorkDetailRaw.description: Unfiltered Protocol.task/1 snapshot and full timeline page behind the detail projection.

WorkItemAssignee.description: PortalJSON owner/1: assignee identity as served, with null members when unset.

WorkItemCommand.description: Protocol.command/1: the task's newest command, any generation. Task-scoped commands (a cancel or retry recorded before any run exists) carry run_id and generation as null; run-scoped commands carry both.

WorkItemDeliveryValue.description: PortalJSON effective_delivery/6: the consumed core is value, source, generation, url and status; provider, recorded_at and other evidence fields stay source-specific and additive.

WorkItemExecution.description: PortalJSON.execution_summary/1 as served when the work item has an orchestration task; null otherwise.

can_cancel.description: True when the task state permits a cancel and, while a runtime holds the attempt (claimed and beyond), that runtime advertises the adapter `cancel` operation; cancel of a queued or assigned attempt is applied by the control plane itself. A runtime without the advertisement is unknown and answers false. A Goal-managed work item always answers false: the legacy cancel path refuses it.

can_retry.description: True when the task state permits a retry, the work item's agent-assignment, external-work and active-project conditions hold, and at least one runtime assignment could select for the goal-less task — same binding as the retry re-admission (the corrected work-item profile and workspace plus the attempt's supervisory requirement) and capability containment, ignoring transient online, heartbeat and capacity state — advertises the adapter `start` operation of the fresh retried attempt. No such runtime answers false. A superseded run's pinned historical entry always answers false.

WorkItemExternal.description: PortalJSON.external_work_item/1 safe display and link fields; raw provider payloads (data, delivery_data) remain additive and unconsumed.

provider_owned_fields.description: Field names the external tracker owns; write refusals still come from Control.

WorkItemOutcome.description: PortalJSON outcome/5: reported execution output with blocker and delivery summary. summary and tests are carried verbatim from the task result or its evidence fallback (legacy payloads may hold objects or strings), while result and failure bodies stay open-ended.

WorkItemTimelineItem.description: Protocol.timeline_page/2 item shared by work detail raw.timeline and the timeline read; data is discriminated on source. Command items carry null run_id and generation when the command is task-scoped, while event and transition items always keep run-scoped identities.

WorkItemWaiting.description: Protocol.waiting/1: current waiting_for_input context; the decision packet stays open because it is carried verbatim from the runtime payload.

WorkItemWaitingDecision.description: Agent-supplied waiting_for_input decision packet; options and recommendation are advisory display data.

WorkspaceWorkItem.description: PortalJSON.work_item/2 as served in workspace rows and work detail reads. The definition body is identical in workspace-read.schema.json and work-detail-read.schema.json so the effect generator shares one graph for both roots; the JSON Schema to TypeScript modules and the quicktype Go output may still restate the shape per root.

can_start.description: True when the work item carries no Goal membership and the legacy launch conditions hold: no orchestration task, an agent assignee, `backlog`/`ready` status, an active project and an available external work item. A Goal-managed work item always answers false: the legacy run endpoint refuses it with `goal_authority_required`.

goal_managed.description: True only when the all-or-nothing Goal membership (goal_id, admitted_revision, acceptance_contract) is set; served so a client can present no writable path for a Goal-managed item.

chat-read.schema.json.description: Consumed fields of SymmetryControl.Chat.conversation/1 (GET /portal/api/chat): the server-resolved scope, the scoped message page and the newest work items' detail projections. Unconsumed presentation fields remain additive.
chat-read.schema.json.title: Symmetry Chat Read v1

payload.description: Operator achieve. An authenticated operator-issued achieve is itself the final operator acceptance for the goal-level operator-acceptance predicate and raises no completion decision for itself. The optional integration_work_item_id carries a server-enforced conditional obligation stated on that property; no caller-controlled required count exists.

integration_work_item_id.description: Optional on the wire; the schema cannot know the persisted required-item cardinality. A contract with exactly one required WorkItem binds that item as the integration item automatically at plan admission and achieve, ignoring optional items; a conflicting pre-marked designation or explicit selection is refused, never ignored or overridden. Every other required-item count still requires this payload, naming the current-revision WorkItem explicitly designated as the integration item.

GoalCompletion.description: The server's completion projection. ready is the same predicate allowed_actions uses to offer achieve; the surface renders it and never recomputes it.

GoalReadAccounting.description: Budget reservation and consumption as served: a held reservation is reservation, known cost is consumption, and unknown consumption stays explicitly unknown rather than zero.

version.description: The durable decision lock version, merged for every served decision from the GoalDecision row (`PortalJSON.goal_decision`); the plan-resolution command presents it as `expected_decision_version`, so a serving-side rename must not silently resolve as null.

GoalReadGraph.description: Read-only dependency projection: nodes, dependency edges with their satisfaction, and the server's cycle flag. No write affordance exists on this surface.

GoalReadGraphEdge.description: One durable work dependency as served. The dependency row has no single-column identity, so id is served as null; from/to carry the work item ids.

GoalReadRevision.description: PortalJSON revision projection: the approved contract members with the revision stamp. The read projection omits the write-side reason/actor_ref and never carries the write schema_version.

goal-read.schema.json.description: Members of the Portal Goal detail read: the existing Goal projection with objective, accepted progress, blockers, the server's own allowed actions, settlement attention, budget reservation and consumption, waiting-external boundaries and the read-only dependency projection. Requiredness here is a per-member pin, not a consumption claim: every member this read requires is one the serving projection always emits (a served null stays nullable), whether or not a surface reads it — the Goal id, blocker_reasons, the completion flags, the accepted-outcome disposition, the graph-edge id and the settlement `required?` member are pinned exactly that way — so omitting or renaming one fails this bundle, the Elixir served-document test and the Effect boundary instead of decoding into a silent fallback. Served members this read leaves optional stay additive, and the client never derives a Goal policy member and never offers an action the served allowed_actions does not list.

allowed_actions.description: The server's exact action list for the rendered version/revision. The surface offers this list and nothing else, with one documented authority exception: an open plan decision whose served options carry `accept` renders the plan-approval control although the read model never lists decision resolution here (a pending plan decision instead suppresses `request_plan`); that control is driven by the served decision itself and the server validates the decision version and the plan admission.

version.description: The Goal's operator-authority version: advanced by exactly one per accepted operator command (creation included) and never by internal reconciliation, settlement or automatic admission. The value every post-creation command must carry as expected_version.

goal-read.schema.json.title: Symmetry Goal Read v1
